messages:
nina (sales): Samir from Summit asked for a minimal, copy/paste runbook for hosted POC keys: short-lived creds, automatic rotation from their CI, plus a revoke endpoint they can call if needed. Can we agree on a recommended pattern?

ash (solutions): Recommended pattern: issue ephemeral key via provisioning API (one-time client_secret), store in customer vault, run nightly CI job to create new key -> validate -> swap -> revoke old key. Use IP allowlist if they want to lock egress. We normally default to 48h for security-sensitive customers unless security approves 72h.

ash (solutions): Minimal create example (curl):
```bash
curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/provision/keys" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PROVISION_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"customer":"summit","type":"ephemeral","ttl_seconds":172800,"scopes":["generation:invoke"],"ip_allowlist":["203.0.113.0/24"]}'
# returns {"key_id":"k_123","client_secret":"s_ABC"} (secret shown once)
```

lina (security): Security checklist: issuance must include audit_tag=poc:summit, client_secret must be vaulted (HSM-backed recommended), rotate every 48h for Summit unless they provide justification for longer. Revoke endpoint: DELETE /v1/keys/{key_id} requires admin token. We'll enable audit retention for this POC.

nina (sales): Samir wants to automate rotation from their CI and receive a webhook callback when a new key is issued. Do we support that?

ash (solutions): Yes, we support an optional rotation_callback URL on create. Callback includes key_id, customer, expires_at, scopes; it never includes the client_secret. Callbacks are HMAC-signed with the provision token. Example create with callback:
```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/provision/keys" \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $PROVISION_TOKEN" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -d '{"customer":"summit","type":"ephemeral","ttl_seconds":172800,"rotation_callback":"https://ci.summit.example/hooks/redwood","ip_allowlist":["203.0.113.0/24"]}'
```

samir.summit (customer): We will run a daily job that: create -> place secret in vault -> run smoke test -> call revoke on old key. For the smoke test, is one small generation call enough?

ash (solutions): Yes, a single lightweight generation request verifying 200 OK is the recommended health-check. If it fails, do not revoke old key. Also ensure the vault update is atomic to avoid race.

deploy-bot: Policy check: issuance_limit=12/hr; required_audit_tag=poc:summit; callback_hmac_required=true.

lina (security): Approved: 48h TTL for Summit, IP allowlist 203.0.113.0/24, callbacks must verify HMAC header. Reminder: do not accept callback URLs that don't validate TLS.

nina (sales): Action items: ash -> provision sample token and final curl for Summit; lina -> enable audit retention and signoff; nina -> send runbook + CI snippet to Samir.

samir.summit (customer): Thanks, please send the runbook. We'll wire the callback and test in staging tomorrow.

ash (solutions): Quick revoke curl (admin):
```bash
curl -X DELETE "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/keys/k_123" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
```

nina (sales): Perfect, I'll email the short playbook now. :thumbsup:
